pk.context: 400 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Relative bioavailability of the tablet is about 80% against a solution, and food does not affect it. Plasma protein binding is 15% to 41%, and about 70% of a dose is eliminated unchanged in urine.
clues.substance: A crystalline powder with a bitter taste and a molecular weight of 339.36.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as tablets of 25, 50, 100, 200, 300 and 400 mg, and as sprinkle capsules.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated with a history of hypersensitivity to the drug or its inactive ingredients; paresthesia and anorexia are among the most frequent reactions.
clues.indication: Epilepsy, including Lennox-Gastaut seizures, and preventive treatment of migraine in patients 12 years and older.
clues.mechanism: Blocks voltage-dependent sodium channels, augments GABA-A receptor activity, antagonizes AMPA/kainate glutamate receptors, and inhibits carbonic anhydrase II and IV.

tell: An anticonvulsant with four proposed mechanisms, also approved for migraine prevention, and cleared mostly unchanged in urine.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: peak plasma concentrations occurring at approximately 2 hours following a 400 mg oral dose
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: The mean plasma elimination half-life is 21 hours
